q: 1. In which sports did Nepal manage to win medals at the 20th Asian Games, 2026?
options: Women's Kabaddi (1 bronze) and Karate (Tenzing Sherpa, 1 bronze)
explain: The Games were held in Nagoya, Japan from 19 September to 4 October 2026. Slogan: Imagine One Asia. 45 nations (including one Asian Refugee Team), 10,787 athletes and 43 sports took part. In the medal table, China was first (169 gold, 89 silver, 83 bronze, total 341), Japan second (83, 95, 91, total 269) and South Korea third (39, 43, 68, total 150). Nepal's flag at the march-past was carried by national women's kabaddi player Manpati Bista and boxer Chandra Bahadur Thapa Magar. This was the third time Japan hosted the Asian Games (earlier in Tokyo in 1958 and Hiroshima in 1994).

q: 2. Who was awarded the Nobel Prize in Medicine in 2026?
options: Francis Halzen (Belgium/USA) and Henri B. Kagan (France)
Karl Deisseroth (USA), Peter Hegemann (Germany) and Georg Nagel (Germany)
Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford (USA)
explain: Karl Deisseroth (USA), Peter Hegemann (Germany) and Georg Nagel (Germany) received the Nobel Prize in Medicine for their important discoveries on light-driven ion channels and optogenetics.

q: 3. Who was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in 2026?
explain: Francis Halzen was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics for his decisive contribution to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos.

q: 4. To which post was Nepal elected at the 11th Annual Meeting of the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB)?
explain: The meeting held in Doha, the capital of Qatar, on 28–29 September 2026 elected Nepal as Vice President from among regional member countries for 2026–27. Nepal, a founding member of the bank, was elected to this post for the first time from among regional members. As the bank provides for one President and one Vice President each from regional and non-regional members, Ireland (from non-regional members) was also selected along with Nepal this time.

q: 5. Who was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 2026?
options: Henri B. Kagan (France) and Kenso Soai (Japan)
Robert E. Hall (USA) and Karl Deisseroth (USA)
explain: Henri B. Kagan (France) and Kenso Soai (Japan) were awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for their discoveries on a special type of chemical process in the creation of organic substances and on spontaneous (auto-)catalysis.

q: 6. Who is the Nepali appointed as head of the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) South Asia Regional Office and Innovation Centre in New Delhi?
explain: Nepali telecommunication and information technology expert Anandraj Khanal has been appointed to the post. Appointed on 22 September 2026, Khanal took charge on 1 October 2026. The jurisdiction of this regional office, established in cooperation with the Government of India, includes Nepal, Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Iran, Maldives and Sri Lanka.

q: 7. Who was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2026?
explain: Anne Carson (Canada) was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature for creating a new dimension and form in contemporary literature through a living dialogue with classical tradition.

q: 8. Which Nepali documentary won the Special Jury Short Documentary Award at the 12th International Films Festival, 2026, held in Shimla, India?
explain: Directed by journalist Ganesh Pandey, the film achieved this success while competing with international documentaries from 33 countries. It captures the adventurous journey to Everest Base Camp of people with serious brain injuries (brain injury survivors) and the story of their struggle. Earlier, the documentary had won the Best Documentary Film Award at the 'Kab' International Film Festival in the USA.

q: 9. Who was awarded the Nobel Prize in Economics in 2026?
options: Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford (USA)
Henri B. Kagan (France) and Kenso Soai (Japan)
explain: Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford (both USA) were awarded the Nobel Prize in Economics for their contribution to strengthening macroeconomic stability.

q: 10. When and where was the 153rd Assembly of the Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU) held?
explain: Nepal was represented at the Assembly in Arusha, Tanzania by Speaker Dip Prasad Aryal. Nepal had tabled the Bhotekoshi flood issue as an emergency proposal, and it secured more than the required two-thirds of votes.

q: 11. How many points does the declaration made public by the 'Women Leadership Summit 2026', held in Koshi Province, contain?
explain: The 'Women Leadership Summit 2026' (B.S. 2083 Baisakh), organized in Biratnagar, Koshi Province, concluded after in-depth discussion on women's leadership, entrepreneurship and economic participation, issuing a 16-point declaration. Entrepreneurs and stakeholders, rather than limiting women to the workforce, stressed skill development, financial access and mentorship to bring them to leadership levels, and pledged to increase women's employment in their organizations.

q: 12. When did the famous Indian actor Nana (Vishwanath) Patekar pass away?
explain: Nana Patekar was born on 1 January 1951 in Maharashtra. His first film was 'Gaman' (1979). He received the Padma Shri honour in 2013.

q: 13. Who is the player who set the record of winning a gold medal at the youngest age in the history of the Asian Games?
options: Yuki Kurihara (11 years, Japan), 20th Asian Games, 2026
explain: Yuki Kurihara, an 11-year-old primary school student from Japan, became the youngest gold medalist at the Asian Games (in 'Puyo Puyo' under e-sports). Kurihara defeated 28-year-old Tanarak Wongkitkun of Thailand in the semi-final and 24-year-old Kang Dohsin of South Korea in the final. He had secured his place to represent Japan at the Asian Games at just 10 years old, and achieved this success while balancing school, extra classes and training. According to the Olympic Council of Asia, Kurihara's win is the record for the youngest gold medal winner in Asian Games history.

q: 14. Who is the thinker who said, 'For happiness, there must be harmony in your thoughts, words and deeds'?
explain: This thought is attributed to Mahatma Gandhi.

q: 15. What was the budget allocation for Nepal's First Five-Year Plan?
explain: The total budget allocated for the First Five-Year Plan (2013-2018 BS) was 33 Crore NPR.

q: 16. How many national languages has the Koshi Province Government recognized as languages of government work?
explain: Besides Nepali, Koshi Province has recognized 13 national languages: Maithili, Limbu, Tharu, Tamang, Magar, Bantawa, Urdu, Rajbanshi, Rai, Newar, Chamling, Sherpa and Santhali.

q: 17. When is Civil Security Day observed in Nepal?
explain: Civil Security Day is observed in Nepal on Asoj 12, and it has been observed since B.S. 2068.

q: 18. Which country was the first to propose the concept of trade liberalization (SAPTA) at the Colombo Summit in 1991?
explain: Sri Lanka first mooted trade liberalization at the 6th Summit in Colombo in December 1991. India, Nepal, and Bangladesh were co-signatories to SAPTA but not the original proposers.

q: 19. When was the National Transport Policy, 2083 approved?
explain: With the approval of the new Transport Policy, 2083, the long-standing National Transport Policy, 2058 has automatically been repealed. The new policy mentions adopting PPP and other suitable models to promote private sector participation in the development of public transport and road infrastructure. Funds received from climate finance, green investment and carbon crediting will be mobilized with priority for developing infrastructure and expanding the system for electric vehicles. To make transport management effective, priority has been given to the Intelligent Transport System (ITS), smart payment systems, and women-, child-, senior citizen- and disability-friendly design principles.

q: 20. The first Earth summit was held at -----------
explain: The United Nations Conference on Environment and Development (UNCED), also known as the Earth Summit, was held in Rio de Janeiro in 1992.

q: 21. --------, came out as a part of Earth Summit 1992.
explain: Agenda 21 is a comprehensive plan of action to be taken globally, nationally, and locally by organizations of the UN, which was a major outcome of the 1992 Earth Summit.

q: 22. When is International Day of Older Persons observed?
explain: The United Nations passed a proposal on 14 December 1990 to observe 1 October as the International Day of Older Persons. On 1 October 2026, the 36th International Day was observed.

q: 23. What is the 'Jitugi' concept related to?
explain: The 'Jitugi' concept is related to foreign employment.

q: 24. When did Finance Minister Dr. Swarnim Wagle make the Economic Status Paper 2083 public?
explain: Finance Minister Dr. Swarnim Wagle made the Economic Status Paper 2083 public on B.S. 2083 Baisakh 14.

q: 25. Which bank was honored as the 'Best Managed Commercial Bank of the Year 2026' at the 10th 'Newbiz Conclave and Business Excellence Awards 2026'?
explain: Everest Bank was honored as the 'Best Managed Commercial Bank of the Year 2026' at the 10th Newbiz Conclave and Business Excellence Awards 2026.

q: 26. The Theme of 'Earth day' 2025 is;
explain: The answer key specifies 'Our Power, Our Planet' as the theme for Earth Day 2025.

q: 27. Which one agenda is not related with Earth Summit, 1992 AD?
explain: Global 500 was an award program started in 1987 by UNEP, whereas the others were formal outcomes or topics of the 1992 Summit.

q: 28. The Goldman award is related to;
explain: The Goldman Environmental Prize is awarded annually to grassroots environmental activists.

q: 29. In which year were all tasks related to the development budget and foreign aid reassigned from the Ministry of Economic Planning to the ministry of finance?
explain: In 1968 (2025 BS), administrative restructuring led to the transfer of budgeting and aid management functions to the Ministry of Finance.

q: 30. At which Summit was the tenure of the Secretary-General formally extended from 2 to 3 years?
explain: The Ninth Summit in Male, Maldives (1997) formally approved extending the tenure to three years. The other options are incorrect.

q:
31. Which of the following Statement(s) about famous Scientist Albert Einstein is/are correct? 
 1. He was born in France 
 2. He received Nobel Prize in 1921 A.D. 
 3. He was died in U.S.A.
explain: Einstein was born in Germany (not France), won the Nobel Prize in 1921 for his work on the photoelectric effect, and died in Princeton, USA.

q: 32. Who is the current chairman of Twitter, the famous social network?
explain: Elon Musk acquired Twitter in 2022 and took over leadership (later rebranding it to X).

q: 33. During the 18th SAARC Summit, which theme has been agreed by all eight member countries by engaging in formal agreement?
explain: At the 18th Summit in Kathmandu, all eight members signed the SAARC Framework Agreement on Energy Cooperation (Electricity).
